prompt:
Structure: Baseball Dashboard dedicated one-game Player Props page for CIN at SF, landscape desktop 1536x1024. Top: a compact dark app header with a small gold tick and “BASEBALL DASHBOARD”, then a breadcrumb “← Back to CIN at SF” and concise game identity row showing CINCINNATI REDS at SAN FRANCISCO GIANTS, Oracle Park, Mon 6:45 PM PDT. Beneath: one shared full-width scoring console titled “LEAN SCORE WEIGHTS” containing three horizontal sliders labeled exactly “Model confidence”, “Statistical edge”, and “Market value”; show weights 40%, 35%, 25% and an explicit “TOTAL 100%”. Include a concise note that cumulative score re-ranks props live. Main: a balanced two-column away/home matchup board divided by a strong central seam, Cincinnati on the left and San Francisco on the right, with each side visually ranking its best props closest to the central seam. This must be a genuinely new dedicated page layout; do not copy the reference screenshot’s split-pane content or layout.

Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web UI product mockup
Input image: Image #1 is a visual-language reference only, never an edit target and never a layout template.
Primary request: Design a data-heavy Operate surface that helps a broad range of baseball bettors understand and compare one-game player-prop leans without resembling a sportsbook bet slip.
Subject: The two-column matchup board contains polished prop rows/cards for realistic players and data. Include Chase Burns, Jung Hoo Lee, Rafael Devers, and Bryce Eldridge. Every prop visibly shows player, prop direction OVER or UNDER, line, American odds, the three factor metrics, one prominent cumulative score, and one concise evidence disclosure. Example realistic content: Chase Burns — OVER 6.5 strikeouts, +100, Model 78, Edge +9.4%, Market +2.1%, score 82, evidence “29.0% K rate · SF projects 24.6%”; Jung Hoo Lee — OVER 0.5 hits, -243, Model 84, Edge +7.8%, Market -1.2%, score 79, evidence “1.1 season avg · favorable contact matchup”; Rafael Devers — OVER 0.5 hits, -159, Model 73, Edge +5.2%, Market +1.7%, score 72; Bryce Eldridge — UNDER 0.5 hits, +115, Model 67, Edge +4.1%, Market +3.0%, score 68. Add several secondary props so the board feels complete and data-rich, but keep hierarchy crisp and best props nearest the central seam. Use a small legend making the cumulative score understandable, not fake predictive claims.
Style/medium: restrained, production-grade flat dashboard UI, high information density, precise alignment, scorecard character, IBM Plex / Barlow-like condensed typography, tabular figures.
Color palette: carry over the incumbent night-game palette exactly in spirit: page #101613, panels #18211c, primary text #e8eae6, gold #e5b54e, coral #e07b6c, blue #82aecf.
Composition/framing: straight-on full-page browser viewport mockup without browser chrome; compact header and controls, then a symmetric two-team comparison board filling the remaining viewport. Strong alignment grid, generous enough spacing for scanning, restrained panel borders, no empty decorative zones.
Text: render the specified interface labels and key player names clearly and legibly.
Constraints: gold eyebrow ticks, hairline rules, flat panels, tabular numbers, visible slider thumbs and filled tracks, explicit total of 100%, cumulative scores ordered, factor labels never ambiguous, concise evidence disclosures. Make the page feel useful to novices while rewarding expert scanning.
Avoid: gradients, glassmorphism, neon, glow, giant typography, decorative hero sections, stadium photography, fake win-rate or certainty claims, sportsbook bet-slip chrome, betting action buttons, casino styling, excessive pills, rounded floating cards, oversized team logos, sidebar layouts, copying the reference split-pane composition, watermarks.
